contexts.story: We’ll start by anchoring the talk in Chao Wang’s own AI journey to show how rapidly the field—and developer roles—have evolved, setting context for why your career strategy must adapt in the LLM era.
Next, we’ll contrast the traditional AI development pipeline with today’s LLM-centric world so you can see how the nature of day-to-day developer work has fundamentally changed.
With that contrast in mind, we’ll walk through a modern LLM-centric development workflow and highlight where the highest-leverage engineering work now happens.
We then translate this workflow shift into a concrete skills roadmap, focusing on the capabilities that most increase your career ROI in the AI era.
To make these skills tangible, we’ll look at practical patterns—prompt tuning and planner–executor architectures—that developers can use to build more reliable LLM-powered systems.
Zooming out, we’ll examine how engineering and applied science roles are converging, why role boundaries are shifting (just like testers did), and how to stay current without burning out.
We’ll close with a simple principle—making every step solid—that ties together technical excellence and long-term career growth in the AI era.
